Find the Bird · 08 August 2026

Golden cutout model report

Nine fully reviewed levels are enough to improve placement and build a useful redo queue. They are not enough to let either model operate without guardrails.

Corpus162 approved birds9 held-out level folds
35 corrections · 126 keeps
27 redos · 132 no-redos
Placement

Ship behind the CLI gate. The portable logistic selector cuts balanced placement loss by 38.9%, halves correction center error, and leaves approved keeps close to their human positions.

Redo prediction

Review queue only. Recall is useful, but 18 of 42 flags are false positives at the normal threshold. It must not automatically spend regeneration credits.

Placement: a guarded improvement

The matcher still generates the candidate box. A level-held-out logistic model decides whether applying that candidate is safer than retaining the current box. This is the important part: keeps are training examples too.

Do nothing

Current box

Perfect on keeps by definition, but only 0.573 IoU and 25.3px center error on human corrections.

Recommended production · best held-out

Safe logistic + hybrid

0.759 correction IoU, 0.979 keep IoU, a 0.60 gate, and a 0.45 normalized movement cap in portable JSON.

Comparison

Shallow forest + hybrid

0.091 balanced loss versus 0.091. It is slightly worse, less portable, and lacks the explicit wrong-neighbor movement guard.

Redo: good ranking, bad autopilot

The positive label means extract the cutout again. It does not mean repaint the scene, and it does not mean regenerate the bird. The reviewed corpus contains zero full-scene regeneration positives.

What is actually in the golden set

Every split is by level, never by bird. Rejected inputs are anchored to an immutable Git commit, blob, and SHA-256; approved outputs and scenes are also content-addressed. One corrected bird is retained as approved but excluded from placement fitting because its exact pre-edit box was overwritten.

Label boundaries

Extraction judges sprite pixels. Placement judges sprite transform. Padding judges the crop sent to extraction. Full-scene regeneration replaces painted content. They are different decisions and the manifest prevents them from being quietly collapsed into one bool.

Limitations

Nine levels are a legitimate hill-climb set, not a final generalization claim. The 35 recoverable corrections are concentrated in a few scenes. Probabilities are useful for ordering, not calibrated enough for billing decisions. Flip metadata is evaluated, but only two flip mismatches occur, so flip learning remains underpowered.

Reproduce it through the editor CLI

All commands are server-free and use the same manifest validation boundary. The model artifacts are portable JSON embedded in the evaluation outputs.

uv run level-editor --json golden-cutouts-validate
uv run level-editor --json golden-cutouts-placement --workers 4 \
  --out eval/results/golden-cutout-v1/placement-evaluation.json
uv run level-editor --json golden-cutouts-evaluate \
  --out eval/results/golden-cutout-v1/redo-evaluation.json
uv run pytest tests/test_golden_cutout_dataset.py tests/test_cli_parity.py -q

Evaluation: leave-one-level-out. Placement objective: class-balanced mean of translation/scale/flip loss on corrected and kept birds. Redo metrics: out-of-fold predictions only. Report generated from content-addressed corpus and checked-in evaluator outputs.
